title: Communications & Engagement Manager
description:
Cumberland Lodge - A place of history and vision

Cumberland Lodge is a beautiful Grade II listed house in Windsor Great Park that has been the home of an educational charity for almost 80 years. Steeped in the nation's history, the Lodge is nestled in the middle of 5,000 acres of ancient royal parkland in the Berkshire countryside.

The foundation was the vision of the academic Amy Buller, whose pioneering work in trying to understand the rise of National Socialism in Germany during the 1930s and its impact on society - especially young people - was presented in her 1943 book Darknessover Germany. Her insights came to the attention of King George VI and Queen Elizabeth (The Queen Mother), who shared her conviction that Britain needed a place of dialogue, understanding, and renewal. Cumberland Lodge was the result.

A living purpose

From this foundation, we continue to convene leaders, students, practitioners, policymakers, and changemakers for residential retreats, conferences, and workshops. These gatherings create the rare conditions for open, respectful debate, helping participants to exchange insights, challenge assumptions, and build understanding across divides.

The Communications and Engagement Manager will work closely with the CEO, Executive, Senior Management Team and Programme Team to:
- Lead on the Lodge's content and engagement work. Recruit and manage time limited senior strategy communications and media support for the 80th anniversary work in 2027.
- Renew and reinvigorate the Communications & Engagement Strategy that supports the strategic objectives set across the organisation and monitor its effectiveness.
- Create proactive content that positively showcases our work, including (but not limited to): news and articles, blogs, e-newsletters, and briefing documents.
- Develop and update the website with content that is engaging, up-to-date and SEO-friendly, to communicate our work, outputs, and impact to our target audiences. Also support the Business Development and Marketing Manager in reviewing the venue hire section.
- Drive forward our social media channels (LinkedIn, Facebook, Instagram, YouTube).
- Produce and edit compelling videos and photography to share on our website and social media.
- Work with the Business Development and Marketing Manager to review any promotional materials for the marketing of Cumberland Lodge as a venue and social enterprise.
- Work proactively with the Programme Team to develop our impact reporting strategy, to include a bank of case studies and testimonials that can be used in print and online.
- Support the Director of Partnerships with fundraising activities to increase awareness of, and engagement with, the work of Cumberland Lodge.
- Ensure that all forms of communication are consistent with our brand, key messages and an appropriate tone of voice.
- Manage the budget for communications, including subscriptions, resource costs, and advertising spend.
- Deliver progress against KPIs and objectives, reporting monthly on these for the CEO, and quarterly for the Board of Trustees.
- Manage and maintain good working relationships with partner organisations and external agencies.
- Provide reactive support to the Executive Team when issues arise.
- Carry out all such other activities as may from time to time be reasonably required

This job description is designed to help you in the understanding of your role and is not intended to be a definitive list of your duties as flexibility in meeting Charity and delegate needs is required by all employees.

This person specification outlines the essential and desirable qualifications, skills, experience, and personal attributes required to successfully perform the role of Communications & Engagement Manager.

Essential
- demonstrable experience of working in a senior role in communications or PR
- a good standard of education, with excellent written and verbal communication skills
- strong storytelling skills, with the ability to shape and adapt content and key messages for different channels and audiences
- experience managing social media platforms, including planning, scheduling, and optimising content to grow engagement and reach.
- experience of managing regular newsletter communications, ideally using email marketing platforms (such as Mailchimp or similar)
- experience of using CMS (such as WordPress or similar), as well as Google Analytics
- experience of video editing software (such as Premier Pro)
- experience of using design software (such as Canva or InDesign)
- experience of monitoring the news agenda to identify relevant content opportunities, and working with colleagues to maximise them
- experience of pitching to/writing for media, and responding to media enquiries, including experience of crisis communications
- the ability to meet tight deadlines, while being able to prioritise a busy workload/manage consecutive projects
- great interpersonal skills, with a welcoming and collaborative approach to working with colleagues across our organisation, ranging from our hospitality teams and chefs, to our programme and finance teams, and senior management

You may also have:
- experience of using social media monitoring platforms (such as Hootsuite)
- a relevant qualification/membership of a professional body (such as CIPR/NCTJ)
- experience of database/contacts management and GDPR compliance
- experience of working with external agencies to deliver key projects.

Salary: £45,000 per annum.

Nature of contract: Full time, permanent, 37.5 hours per week.

Location: Four days per week in the office, one day working from home. You will need access to a vehicle, and live within a circa 45-minute radius, as Cumberland Lodge is located remotely in Windsor Great Park without easy access by public transport.

Due to the residential and 24/7 nature of the organisation, this role may require some evening and weekend working.

Additional benefits:
- Pension: Standard Life contributory pension (up to, and currently, 10% organisational contributions to support 5% personal contributions, with the option to increase personal contributions above 5%).
- 25 days' annual leave plus eight days standard UK bank holidays.
- Annualised hours working pattern.
- Lunch provided on-site.
- Death in service benefit four x salary after probation period.
- Employee support benefits, includes access to a virtual GP service and mental health support.
